correctness.summary: The leading-residue theorem and no-join mechanism are correct. The localization hypothesis E=R[t^{-1}] together with 1 notin tR forces the t-adic intersection of R to be zero, so every nonzero x has a finite maximal t-depth. After normalization, positivity is exactly the condition that the first nonzero residue lies in F_{>0}. If x in R\tR has residue outside F and u is a common upper bound of 0 and x, then u cannot lie in R; writing u=t^{-n}(a+tr) with n>=1 and a>0 shows that every scalar multiple lambda u with 0<lambda<1 remains a common upper bound while being strictly smaller. Thus incomparable pairs have neither minimal common upper bounds nor maximal common lower bounds. Totality is therefore equivalent to R/tR being exactly F. In that case every element outside tR is a unit and every nonzero element is a unit times a power of t, so R is a DVR. The finite-extension corollary follows from the standard sum e_i f_i=[L:K] in the separable case.

limitations: The theorem classifies only the stated localization-cone construction and does not resolve the Birkhoff–Pierce problem for arbitrary lattice orders on C.
The finite-extension corollary uses the integral closure of a DVR in a finite separable extension; immediate infinite extensions are outside that corollary.
The valuation-theoretic ingredients and the implication division-closed lattice field => total order are classical.
The source construction is very recent, so unindexed parallel refinements remain a priority risk.

originality.summary: Wang–Yuan–Zhang–Zhu's September 2026 preprint supplies the localization cones, directedness, inversion closure and examples that are not lattice orders. Classical ordered-ring work already shows that a division-closed lattice-ordered field must be totally ordered. Targeted current searches did not locate the exact residue-level comparability criterion, the statement that every incomparable pair has no minimal common upper bound, or the equivalence with the DVR boundary for this localization construction. Originality is therefore supported narrowly as a structural classification of a very recent construction; valuation-order and lattice-field background are prior art.

scientific_value.summary: The record upgrades isolated nonlattice examples to a complete first-residue obstruction and cleanly identifies the only total/lattice case. The DVR and finite-algebraic-extension corollaries make the boundary algebraically transparent. Its scope is the localization-cone family, not arbitrary directed orders on fields.
